title: Annual Dry Bulk Market Review 2026
text: Iron ore remains the largest single dry bulk cargo by volume, followed by coal and grains. China accounted for roughly 70% of global seaborne iron ore imports in 2025. Demand for dry bulk shipping is therefore closely tied to Chinese steel production. Grain trade grew modestly, supported by South American export volumes.

title: Port Throughput Statistics Digest, Q4 2025
text: Chinese iron ore imports reached a record 1.21 billion tonnes in 2025. Coal imports declined slightly year on year as domestic production increased. Iron ore remains the dominant inbound dry bulk commodity at major Chinese ports.

title: Technical Note: Fleet Efficiency Regulations and Operating Speeds
text: The EEXI and CII rules are expected to lead many older vessels to reduce operating speeds, lowering effective fleet capacity. Owners of vessels rated D or E under CII must submit corrective action plans. Slower steaming reduces the number of voyages each ship can complete per year.

title: Weekly Dry Bulk Market Report
text: The orderbook stands at 7% of the fleet, the lowest level in over two decades. With limited new supply, we expect rates to firm through 2027. Longer trade routes are adding to tonne-miles, which absorbs available capacity.

title: Dry Bulk Supply Outlook
text: Our fleet database shows an orderbook-to-fleet ratio of roughly 10%, higher than commonly cited figures once smaller handysize orders are included. Newbuilding deliveries are set to rise in 2027 as yards complete contracts signed in 2024 and 2025.

title: Shipping Sector Note: Capesize Outlook
text: Continued contraction in Chinese property construction is weighing on steel demand. As a result, we expect average Capesize rates to fall in 2027 compared with 2026. Infrastructure spending provides only partial offset.

title: Atlas Mining Targets Higher Iron Ore Exports
text: Atlas Mining expects its iron ore exports to grow 5% next year, the company said in a statement. The miner cited new port capacity and strong customer demand in Asia.

title: Miner Atlas Sees Export Growth
text: In a press release on Monday, Atlas Mining said it expects iron ore exports to rise by 5% next year. The company pointed to expanded port capacity and firm Asian demand.

title: Trade Route Disruptions and Bulk Shipping
text: Red Sea diversions have lengthened average voyage distances, increasing tonne-miles demand. Low water levels at the Panama Canal have also forced some bulk carriers onto longer routes. A reopening of these routes would release capacity back into the market.

title: Re: Where are bulker rates heading??
text: Trust me, rates will triple next year, guaranteed. Everyone who is not buying bulker stocks now will regret it.

title: Dry Bulk Outlook 2019
text: The orderbook stands at 12% of the fleet, and deliveries over the next two years will add meaningful new capacity. We expect supply growth to outpace demand growth in 2019.

title: Bulk Carrier Basics for New Investors
